workflow_name: Expenses document date for later period v/s posting date in previous period / qtr
workflow_description: Flag line items where Document Date falls in a later accounting month-year than Posting Date, including across years, indicating potential timing irregularities.
business_logic_plan: Business Logic Plan: Expenses document date for later period v/s posting date in previous period / qtr Data Source List each required file and its columns: Required File 1: data/uploads/ea2e91f9-f77a-4ee8-ae6f-c65004798cea/FBL3N.csv Required Columns: ["Document Date", "Posting Date"] Requirements List every question asked (without the multiple choice options) and the user's answer: Q1: Which base exception rule should we apply when comparing 'Document Date' vs 'Posting Date'? A1: Flag every record where the month-year of 'Document Date' is later than the month-year of 'Posting Date' (strictly later by any amount of months). Q2: Which records should be evaluated for this exception rule? A2: No answer provided. Business Logic Detailed step-by-step logic that a data analyst can follow to implement this workflow in code: Step 1: Load data from data/uploads/ea2e91f9-f77a-4ee8-ae6f-c65004798cea/FBL3N.csv into a dataframe named fbl3n_df. Step 2: Ensure columns required for this workflow are present: - Confirm the presence of "Document Date" and "Posting Date". - If either column is missing, stop the workflow and raise an error indicating the missing column(s). Step 3: Convert date columns to date/datetime types: - Parse fbl3n_df["Document Date"] and fbl3n_df["Posting Date"] into datetime objects. - Use a consistent date parser and set errors to coerce invalid values to NaT. - Retain the original string values if needed, but all subsequent logic must use the parsed datetime columns. Step 4: Handle null or invalid dates: - Create a boolean column "Has_Valid_Dates" that is True only when both "Document Date" and "Posting Date" are not NaT. - Exclude rows with Has_Valid_Dates = False from exception evaluation (they cannot be assessed). Optionally keep them in the base dataframe with Exception_Flag set to "N" and Month_Diff set to null. Step 5: Derive accounting month-year components: - Create integer columns: - "Posting_Year" = year(Posting Date) - "Posting_Month" = month(Posting Date) - "Document_Year" = year(Document Date) - "Document_Month" = month(Document Date) - Create normalized month-year string columns: - "Posting_MonthYear" = format as "YYYY-MM" from Posting_Year and Posting_Month (zero-pad month to 2 digits). - "Document_MonthYear" = format as "YYYY-MM" from Document_Year and Document_Month (zero-pad month to 2 digits). Step 6: Compute month difference to capture across-year timing: - Create integer column "Month_Diff" = (Document_Year - Posting_Year) * 12 + (Document_Month - Posting_Month). Step 7: Apply the base exception rule confirmed by the user: - Create column "Exception_Flag" with values: - "Y" if Month_Diff > 0 (i.e., Document month-year is strictly later than Posting month-year, including across years). - "N" otherwise (Month_Diff <= 0). - Create a text column "Exception_Reason": - If Exception_Flag = "Y": "Document Date month-year is later than Posting Date month-year." - Else: empty string. Step 8: Determine evaluation population based on Q2: - Since no filter choice was provided, evaluate all line items by default (no additional filtering by G/L account, account type, etc.). - If a population filter is later specified, apply it before computing final exceptions and re-run Steps 5–7 on the filtered data. Step 9: Create the final exceptions dataframe: - Filter fbl3n_df to rows where Exception_Flag = "Y" and Has_Valid_Dates = True. - Select the output columns listed in the Output Dataframe Structure section below. - Optionally sort by "Posting Date" ascending, then "Document Date" ascending, and then by "Month_Diff" descending to prioritize larger gaps. Step 10: Quality checks: - Verify that all rows in the exceptions output have Month_Diff > 0. - Spot-check edge cases (e.g., Posting Date in December and Document Date in January of next year) to ensure Month_Diff is positive and the record is flagged. Output Dataframe Structure List each output column with its description: Document Date: Original document date from FBL3N.csv, parsed as a date; used to compute document month-year. Posting Date: Original posting date from FBL3N.csv, parsed as a date; used to compute posting month-year. Posting_Year: Four-digit year extracted from Posting Date. Posting_Month: Numeric month (1–12) extracted from Posting Date. Posting_MonthYear: Normalized month-year string for Posting Date in the format "YYYY-MM". Document_Year: Four-digit year extracted from Document Date. Document_Month: Numeric month (1–12) extracted from Document Date. Document_MonthYear: Normalized month-year string for Document Date in the format "YYYY-MM". Month_Diff: Integer month difference calculated as (Document_Year - Posting_Year) * 12 + (Document_Month - Posting_Month); positive values indicate the document month-year is later. Exception_Flag: "Y" if Month_Diff > 0, otherwise "N". Exception_Reason: Text explanation populated when Exception_Flag = "Y" ("Document Date month-year is later than Posting Date month-year.").
